sections.h2: Selling a house in the city of Chester
sections.html:
Chester is a dense river city in Delaware County, and a sale there turns on three local things: an old housing stock, a city under state financial oversight, and a transfer tax higher than the usual local rate. The city lies along the Delaware River's western shore, between Philadelphia and Wilmington, with 4.83 square miles of land. Streets run on a grid, with numbered streets east and west and named streets north and south.

An owner here has three routes: hire an agent, negotiate privately with a buyer, or take an as-is cash purchase. The right one turns on the roof, plumbing and wiring, any unpaid taxes, and your deadline.

Much of Chester's housing was built for a larger workforce, when the population peaked at 66,039 in 1950. The count was 32,605 in 2020, and the estimate for 2025 is 33,996. What remains is mostly rowhouses and twins on narrow lots, many a century old. Buyers and inspectors tend to look closely at foundations, old heating systems, lead paint and aging sewer laterals.

Chester is low and sits where Chester Creek and Ridley Creek reach the Delaware River, so flood exposure varies a lot by block. Damp basements, sump pumps and old drainage are routine inspection topics. Find out whether your address is in a mapped flood zone and whether the house carries flood insurance before you list, since a buyer's lender will check the same thing.

There are more renters than owners, and values are well below the nearby suburbs. A buyer looking at a Chester rowhouse is comparing it with other Chester rowhouses.

With 60 percent of households renting, many houses are investor-owned or have a tenant living in them. Sellers with occupied units should plan around the tenant's lease and the city's rental registration rules below.

Pennsylvania designated Chester a financially distressed municipality in 1995, declared a fiscal emergency in 2020, and in 2022 the city filed for Chapter 9 bankruptcy. The recovery process is still part of local government, with a receiver and an advisory committee.

The effect on a seller lands on the tax side more than on the sale. Property tax rates and city fees can change as the recovery plan is revised, so an old tax bill is a weak guide to what the next owner will carry. Ask the City of Chester finance office for the current city millage, and ask the Delaware County treasurer for the county and school figures, when you work out your net.

None of this stops a sale. A title company wants a clean tax picture, so unpaid city bills, rubbish fees and liens should be sorted out before settlement.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Chester sale
sections.html:
Chester charges 1.5 percent on the city side, effective September 1, 2023, on top of the 1 percent that goes to the Commonwealth. That is 2.5 percent of the sale price in total. The Delaware County Recorder of Deeds treats Chester as one of four municipalities above the standard local rate, the others being Radnor, Upper Darby and Upper Providence.

Under state rules the grantor and the grantee share legal liability, so the agreement of sale should name who pays. Certain family transfers and inherited property are exempt. For a doubtful case, the county refers questions to the state revenue department's realty transfer tax unit.

The city's Licenses and Inspections department, known as L&I, handles permits, rental registration and several exemption forms. Its page lists the forms a seller or landlord is most likely to touch.

  • Building permit application and the residential permit fee schedule
  • Rental registration application, FAQ, letter and a residential rental licensing policy summary
  • Use and occupancy fee schedule and a commercial use and occupancy permit form
  • Contractor license application
  • Homeowner exemption form and a senior citizen disability exemption form for residential property

If the house is rented, find out whether the unit is registered before you list it, because a buyer's lender or title agent may ask. If you did work on the house without a permit, contact L&I at City Hall before you market the property. Open permits are easier to close out while you still control the building.

The city assessor's page also posts conditions and bid forms for repository properties, which are parcels that did not sell at county tax sales, and a LERTA application for tax abatement on improvements.

Chester property is assessed by Delaware County. The county's tax bill is mailed on February 1, and paying within 60 days earns a 2 percent discount. After April 1 the bill is due at face value by June 1. Chester Upland School District covers the city, Chester Township and Upland borough.

The county's Homestead and Farmstead Exclusion lowers the assessed value on a primary residence. The application comes from your school district, and the window runs every year from December 15 to March 1. If you are about to sell, the exclusion matters more to the buyer, who will need to apply in their own name.

An assessment challenge is filed at the Board in Media, on paper with an original signature. Faxed or e-mailed forms are rejected, and since postmarks can lag, hand delivery or a counter receipt at the post office is safer. If you disagree with the Board's findings, you have 30 days to go to court. The notice you were mailed gives the filing date.

Putting the house on the market gives the widest exposure but needs showings, repairs and a lender's approval, which can stretch the timeline by months. An investor or cash purchase gives up some price for speed and certainty, and the buyer generally accepts the property with its flaws.

  • Inherited house with several heirs: confirm who holds title and whether the estate is open before accepting any offer
  • Tenant in place: read the lease and plan for notice requirements
  • Back taxes or city liens: get payoff figures from the county and the city
  • Code or permit issues: ask L&I what is open on the address

Whatever you pick, line up the offers by the check you would actually receive after transfer tax, payoffs and credits.

Collect the latest county and school tax bills, any city rubbish or rental registration notices, and written payoff figures for liens. Ask L&I whether the address has open permits. Confirm who signs the deed if title is shared among heirs. A seller with these in hand gives the title agent less to chase, and the settlement date holds.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax if I sell a house in Chester?
faqs.a: The combined rate is 2.5 percent: 1 percent to the state and 1.5 percent to the local side, which has applied in Chester since September 1, 2023. The contract decides who pays, though the state holds both parties responsible.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Chester house that has a tenant living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. The lease usually continues with the new owner unless it ends or the tenant agrees to leave. Check whether the unit is registered with the city's L&I department before you list.

faqs.q: Who do I ask about property taxes on a Chester house?
faqs.a: Start with the Delaware County treasurer and Board of Assessment in Media for county and school figures, and the City of Chester finance office for city charges. Both can confirm balances before closing.

faqs.q: Does Chester's bankruptcy stop me from selling?
faqs.a: No. Houses sell in Chester under the same Pennsylvania rules as elsewhere. The recovery process mainly affects city tax rates and fees, so call for current figures before you price the house.

faqs.q: How do I claim the homestead exclusion on a Chester home?
faqs.a: Request the application from the Chester Upland School District between December 15 and March 1, then send it to the county Board of Assessment in Media. The county replies within 30 days.
